content.content:
### Move, scale and rotate

| Gesture | What it does |
|---|---|
| Drag inside the box | Move. Every selected clip moves by the same amount |
| ← → ↑ ↓ (canvas focused) | Nudge the selection 1 canvas pixel |
| ⇧ + arrow | Nudge 10 pixels |
| Drag one of the eight square handles | Scale (see below) |
| ⌥ while scaling | Scale about the centre instead of pinning the opposite handle |
| Drag the round grip above the top edge | Rotate about the clip's centre |
| ⇧ while rotating | Snap the angle to 15° steps |
| Esc during any drag | Cancel the drag and put the clip back where it was, with no undo step |

How a scale drag behaves depends on the clip:

- **Video, image, still, graphic and nest clips** have one uniform scale. Every
  handle scales the whole picture and keeps its aspect ratio.
- **Shape clips** change their box size instead. A corner handle keeps the
  aspect ratio and ⇧ frees it. An edge handle changes only the width or only
  the height.
- **Text clips**: the left and right edge handles set the text box's wrap
  width, which makes the box fixed-width. The corners and the top and bottom
  edges scale the text uniformly.

A drag scales between 1 % and 1000 %. Each drag is one undo step, and a click
that doesn't move anything adds no step.

There is no separate anchor-point control. Rotation, the Picture tab's Scale
field and a ⌥ scale drag pivot on the centre of the clip's uncropped picture.
A plain handle drag keeps the opposite handle in place by moving the clip as
it scales.

### Line and arrow endpoints

A line or arrow shape has a round handle at each end. Drag a handle to move
that end. The scale handles and the rotation grip still work on the line's
box.

### Snapping

While you drag a clip to move it, the box snaps to:

- the canvas edges, its centre lines and its thirds
- the edges and centres of every other visible layer

Scaling, rotating and cropping do not snap (⇧ while rotating snaps the angle
to 15° steps instead). A guide line is drawn across the canvas on each axis that snapped. Press
**N** or choose **View ▸ Snapping** to turn snapping on or off. The timeline
uses the same setting. Hold ⌘ during a drag to stop snapping for that drag.

### Safe areas

**View ▸ Safe Areas**, or the toolbar's **Safe** checkbox, draws two guide
frames over the canvas, at 90 % and 80 % of its size. They are guides only
and never appear in an export. The app remembers the setting.

### Editing an action's end state on the canvas

With an action selected on the clip's action lane, a move, scale, rotate or
crop drag, or an arrow-key nudge, edits that action's end state, just as the
inspector's fields do. The box on screen still shows the frame at the
playhead. There are two exceptions: a drag on a multi-clip selection, and a
shape's box resize, both edit the clip itself. See
[Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

## Crop

Press **C**, or double-click a clip that is not text, to enter crop mode for
the selected clip. The eight handles become crop edges, and the part being
cut away is shown as a dim ghost inside the uncropped frame. Press **Esc** or
**Return**, or click empty canvas, to leave crop mode.

A crop removes edges in place: the picture never shifts as you crop. Crop
amounts are in the source's own pixels, so they stay correct when you scale
the clip later. The core keeps at least one source pixel in each direction.

The Picture tab's **Crop** section has the same four insets as fields, plus a
**Crop on Canvas** button that enters crop mode. Crop appears only for clips
with pixels of their own, which means video, image and still clips.

## The Picture tab

Select a clip and open the inspector's **Clip** tab. Its sub-tabs depend on
what is selected:

- Text clips start on **Text** and shapes on **Shape**.
- Any clip that draws has **Picture**.
- **Color**, **Sound** and **Clip** follow where they apply.

An adjustment clip has no Picture tab, because it has no picture of its own
(see [Color grading](color-grading.md)).

Picture's sections, in order:

| Section | Shown for |
|---|---|
| Transform | every clip that draws |
| Behind Subject | every clip that draws but an adjustment or nest clip, at the top level |
| Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key | video, image and still clips |
| Background | clips of a video file, freeze frames of one, and image clips |
| Cursor | clips of a movie whose cursor file the picture doesn't already show ([The cursor](screen-recording.md#the-cursor)) |
| Shadow, Filters, Reflection, Spotlight, Obscure | every clip that draws, text and shapes included |

Each section folds open and shut and shows a one-line summary while closed.
Transform starts open. **Reset** appears only while a section differs from its
default. With several clips selected, a field shows the first clip's value and
a mixed badge when the others differ. An edit applies to every selected clip.
Colour swatches open the macOS Colors panel, with opacity.

*Agents:* `set_video` (merges a patch into each clip's video properties: `x`,
`y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `blend`, `crop`, `corner_radius`,
`shadow`, `chroma`, `filters`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `obscure`).

### Transform

| Row | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Scale | 1–1000 % (quick values 25–400) | 100 % |
| Position X / Y | −20000 to 20000 canvas px, measured from the canvas centre, X right and Y down | 0, 0 |
| Rotation | −180° to 180° | 0° |
| Opacity | 0–100 % | 100 % |
| Blend | the eight blend modes below | Normal |
| Motion Blur | 0–100 % of a frame (quick values 0, 25, 50, 100); greyed on a nest or adjustment clip ([Motion blur](motion-and-transitions.md#motion-blur)) | 0 % |

Two buttons sit under the rows:

- **Fit to Canvas** scales each clip so its whole picture fits, and centres it.
- **Fill Canvas** scales each clip until it covers the whole canvas, and
  centres it.

Text clips are skipped, because their size comes from the words. Reset
Transform sets position, scale, rotation, opacity, blend and motion blur back to
their defaults.

#### Blend modes

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| Normal | Draws over what is underneath |
| Multiply | Darkens by multiplying with what is underneath |
| Screen | Lightens, the inverse of multiply. A screened white blob reads as a glow |
| Add | Adds the colours together |
| Overlay | Multiplies the darks and screens the lights |
| Darken | Keeps the darker of the two colours |
| Lighten | Keeps the lighter of the two colours |
| Difference | The absolute difference of the two colours |

A blend needs something under the layer. Over the empty black canvas,
Multiply, Darken and Overlay read black, and Screen, Add, Lighten and
Difference change nothing. When that is what is happening, the section says
so, for example "Nothing behind this clip — multiply reads black here." The
note looks at the clip's whole span, not just the playhead. It ignores hidden
tracks and clips with their video turned off, and it appears only while the
canvas background is opaque black. To get a layer to blend against, use
**Clip ▸ Add Background** (see [Backgrounds](#backgrounds)), or set a
non-black canvas background on the Document tab. The Blend popup's tooltip
gives the same explanation.

Limits:

- A cross dissolve draws as Normal for as long as the clips overlap.
- The Blend popup is greyed on a nest clip, because a nest has no pixels of its
  own to blend. Un-nest it (⇧⌘G) to blend the clips inside.
- Blend is an ordinary property, so an action can change it. Like any
  on/off-style value, the change happens at the action's end.

### Corner Radius

Radius: 0–500 px in source pixels (quick values 0–64). It rounds the cropped
picture's corners. Default 0.

## Limits

- Scale is uniform for pictures. Only shapes (box width and height) and text
  (wrap width) can be stretched on one axis.
- At most four filters and four obscure regions per clip. Gradients have 2–8
  stops.
- Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key are only for video, image and still
  clips.
- A nest clip can't take a blend mode, and Add Blurred Background is not
  offered for one.
- Locked tracks can't be edited on the canvas, and hidden tracks can't be
  clicked there.
- The canvas text editor stays upright even for a rotated text clip. The text
  you apply is the same either way.
19:| Colours (shadow, chroma key, text colours, word-caption colours, a graphic's colour properties) | Ramp in OKLab, which keeps the blend's midpoints even. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact |
22:| Curves | Always animate. Two curves with the same number of points ramp point by point; a neutral curve lines up with the other curve's points; two curves with different numbers of points blend their values over the action |
296:A blended clip blends its averaged picture once: a screened clip, for example,
379:None removes the stored transition but not the overlap. While two clips still overlap they keep blending as a plain linear dissolve, with no hatch on the timeline. To get a hard cut back, move or trim the clips so they no longer overlap.
389:- A layer always blends normally while it is in a transition, whatever blend mode it has.

| Numbers (position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, volume, a filter's amount, a grade's sliders, a graphic's number properties) | Ramp along the action's curve |
| Colours (shadow, chroma key, text colours, word-caption colours, a graphic's colour properties) | Ramp in OKLab, which keeps the blend's midpoints even. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact |
| Switches, popups and text (an on/off box, a filter's kind, a font, a graphic's string, boolean or image property) | Hold, then switch to the end value when the action ends |
| Lists (filters, obscure regions) | Ramp entry by entry while both ends have the same number of entries. If the list's length changes, the whole list switches at the end. If one entry changes kind (or a region its shape), only that entry switches at the end and the others still ramp |
| Curves | Always animate. Two curves with the same number of points ramp point by point; a neutral curve lines up with the other curve's points; two curves with different numbers of points blend their values over the action |

The four curves are the same everywhere an action or a transition is eased:

| Curve | Lane label | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| Linear | Linear | Constant speed |
| Ease In | In | Starts slowly, ends fast |
| Ease Out | Out | Starts fast, ends slowly |

Changes the clips' BASE video properties — position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corner radius, shadow, colour, chroma key, filters, reflection, spotlight and motion (what the clip does on its way in, on its way out and all the way through). The patch MERGES AT EVERY DEPTH: keys you leave out keep their values, inside a nested object too — a patch of just {shadow: {blur: 20}} keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance — and shadow, chroma, reflection, spotlight or motion set to null clears it. A LIST is the exception: filters and obscure each replace whole, so send the whole stack and [] to clear it. A key or a value the vocabulary does not have is an error naming its dotted path (array indices included) and the value you sent; nothing is dropped, corrected or clamped. Placement is spec §5.3: the source rectangle is centred at the canvas centre plus (x, y), scaled, then rotated about that centre, and crop removes edges in place without shifting the content. To animate a property instead, add_action and then set_action_end. # app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.

- `GraphicStore.swift` — one document's `graphics/` (road map 10 §5f):
  where it is (`<package>/graphics`, or an untitled document's
  `<NSTemporaryDirectory()>/FrameJob/<UUID>-graphics`, re-pointed by
  `packageDidMove(to:)` from the `fileURL` setter, posting
  `.graphicsLocationDidChange`), the scan (each legal `*.js` with its
  SHA-256 revision, G-13; `fonts/` validated on a throwaway
  `GraphicLibrary` once per file identity — size, modification date and
  file number — in `GraphicStore+Fonts.swift`'s `validatedFonts`, whose
  `fontVerdicts` is queue-confined and survives `stop()`/`start()` (spec

  cannot use, warned and skipped, G-23 (e)) and the watch. **`graphics/` is created on the app's first write, never at
  open** (G-14): `ensureFolder()` is the ONE creator inside a package, and
  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is
  refused as "changed by another application". A folder source raises
  `.write` only and an in-place save raises nothing on it (G0 q7), so each
  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11
  G-19 (c), G-20 (a)); a source whose `open` fails is a scan warning,
  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).
  `GraphicStore+Files.swift` holds the store's own writes:
  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.
  `write(name:bytes:)` is `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are, and
  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.
  `GraphicStore+History.swift` is the kept revisions and the rename journal
  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.
  `history/` is created only inside an existing `graphics/` (G-14) with no
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` call, and `moveHistory` leaves no
  `history/<from>/` behind — which is what makes 'no file, something kept'
  mean a DELETED module. `GraphicStore+Import.swift`'s `importAsset` files a name
  `asset(name)` cannot use under `GraphicAssetName.legalized`, a renamed
  copy taking `-2`, `-3`, … while `holdsAsset(named:)` (scan or disk) says
  the name is held, and answers `name`/`renamedFrom` (G-23 (c), (d)).
  `landNew` is the `.fjgraphic` import's write (G-47 (e)): bytes landed
  under a name not yet taken, never replacing a file. **`drain()` is not
  re-entrant: never call `rescan()` from a `.graphicsDidChange` observer.**
  `stop()` bumps a generation under `queue.sync`. `makeLibrary()` is a NEW
  builder every call (a library freezes on first use). It also writes the
  app's bundled reference into an EXISTING folder as `API.md` and `API.d.ts`
  (`writeManual()`, from `start()` for a saved package, `ensureFolder()` and
  `write()`; only when the bytes differ) — never a reason to create the
  folder (G-14).

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`

  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and

  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of

  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.

  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or

  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a

  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2

  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`

  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is

  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and

  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

---
title: Crop
description: Trim a picture's edges by dragging handles on the canvas or by typing an exact number of pixels.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Crop cuts pixels off the edges of a video, image or still clip. Drag the edges on the canvas when you're working by eye, or type the amounts when you need them exact.

<AtAGlance
  keys="C"
  where={['Double-click a clip in the preview', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Crop']}
  tools="set_video"
/>

## Crop mode

Crop mode turns the handles on the canvas into crop edges.

<Steps>

1. Select the clip, with the playhead somewhere it's showing.

2. Press <kbd>C</kbd>, double-click the clip in the preview, or choose **Crop on Canvas** in the Crop section.

3. Drag the [crop handles](#crop-handles).

4. Press <kbd>↩</kbd> to [leave crop mode](#leaving-crop-mode).

</Steps>

<kbd>C</kbd> beeps when no selected clip is showing at the playhead, because there's nothing on the canvas to crop. Double-clicking a text clip opens its text editor instead.

Going in and out of crop mode isn't an edit, so it adds nothing to undo.

## Crop handles

In crop mode the eight square handles become crop edges and the rotation grip goes away. A corner handle moves two edges, and a side handle moves one.

What you're cutting away shows as a dim ghost, inside a dashed outline of the uncropped frame.

- A drag changes the crop and nothing else. The clip's position stays put, and the picture doesn't shift.
- A crop drag doesn't snap.
- At least one source pixel always remains in each direction, however far you drag.
- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during a drag to cancel it. The crop goes back to where it was, with no undo step.
- Each finished drag is one undo step.

Dragging inside the box still moves the clip, as it does outside crop mode. With several clips selected, the handles belong to the front-most one and crop only that clip.

## Leaving crop mode

Your crop stays when you leave. Any of these leaves crop mode:

| Do this | Good to know |
| --- | --- |
| Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Needs the canvas to have focus. |
| Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Needs the canvas to have focus. During a drag, the first <kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels the drag and the next one leaves the mode. |
| Press <kbd>C</kbd> or choose **Crop on Canvas** | Works wherever the focus is, except while you're typing in a field. |
| Click empty canvas | This also clears the selection, unless you hold <kbd>⇧</kbd>. |
| Click a different clip on the canvas | That clip becomes the selection. |

The canvas has focus once you've clicked or dragged on it. If you pressed <kbd>C</kbd> and haven't touched the canvas yet, press <kbd>C</kbd> again to leave.

Crop mode also ends if nothing selected is left on the canvas, for example when you clear the selection in the timeline.

## The Crop section

The **Crop** section on the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) has the same four edges as fields, for when you want an exact number. It shows only for video, image and still clips.

| Field | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Left** | Source pixels cut from the left edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
| **Top** | Source pixels cut from the top edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
| **Right** | Source pixels cut from the right edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
| **Bottom** | Source pixels cut from the bottom edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |

These are typed fields, with no slider. **Crop on Canvas** under them goes in and out of crop mode.

Closed, the section's summary reads `none`, or the four amounts in field order, such as `100·0·100·0`. **Reset** appears in the section's header while there's a crop, and takes all four edges back to 0.

Left and Right together must stay under the picture's width, and Top and Bottom under its height. If a number would use up the whole picture, Frame Job shows an error and keeps the crop you had.

:::caution
With several clips selected, editing one field gives every clip all four of the first clip's amounts, not only the edge you changed. Crop clips of different sizes one at a time.
:::

## How a crop works

A crop removes edges in place. The picture you keep stays exactly where it was on the canvas, so cropping the left edge opens a gap on the left rather than sliding the picture over.

The amounts are in the source's own pixels, not canvas pixels, so they stay correct when you scale the clip later. Cutting 100 px from a clip at 50 % takes 50 canvas pixels off it, and the same 100 px at 200 % takes 200.

Position, scale and rotation go on measuring from the centre of the uncropped picture. A crop doesn't recentre what's left, so move the clip if you want that.

- [Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas](/canvas/transform/#fit-and-fill) measure the uncropped picture too.
- [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/) and the [shadow](/effects/shadow/) follow the cropped edge.
- [Reset in Transform](/canvas/transform/#reset) leaves the crop alone.

## Animate a crop

A crop can change over time. With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected on a single clip, a crop handle or a field sets the crop at the action's end, and the edges move there along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

While you're editing an action, the section's **Reset** gives way to **Clear**, which takes the crop out of that action.

## Good to know

- Crop mode has no menu item. It's <kbd>C</kbd>, a double-click, or the **Crop on Canvas** button.
- <kbd>C</kbd> also opens crop mode on a text, shape, graphic or nest clip, and a double-click does on all of those except text. They have no Crop section, so there are no fields and no **Reset**. To take that crop off, undo or drag the handles back.
- A clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) shows no crop handles.

## Related

- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)
- [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/)
- [The Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/)

---
title: The Picture tab
description: Find every section of the Clip tab's Picture sub-tab, see which clips get which section, and learn how the sections behave.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Picture tab is where you place a clip in the frame and style what it draws. It's one sub-tab of the inspector's **Clip** tab, and the sections it shows depend on what you've selected.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture" tools="set_video" />

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with a video clip selected and its Picture sub-tab chosen beside Color, Sound and Clip. The Transform section is open, with rows for Scale, Position X, Position Y, Rotation, Opacity, Blend and Motion Blur, then the Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas buttons. Behind Subject and Layout sit below it."
/>

## Open the Picture tab

Select a clip, open the inspector's **Clip** tab and choose **Picture**. A video or image clip opens on it, while a text clip opens on **Text**, a shape on **Shape** and a graphic on **Graphic**.

The sub-tabs you get depend on the clip:

| Selected | Sub-tabs |
| --- | --- |
| Video clip | Picture, Color, Sound, Clip |
| Image or still clip | Picture, Color, Clip |
| Text clip | Text, Picture, Clip |
| Shape clip | Shape, Picture, Clip |
| Graphic clip | Graphic, Picture, Clip |
| Nest clip | Picture, Clip |
| Adjustment clip | Color, Clip |
| Clip of an audio-only file | Sound, Clip |

**Sound** joins the list for any clip with live audio, so a video clip with no sound doesn't have it and a nest with sound inside does.

A selection with an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) in it has no Picture tab, because an adjustment clip draws nothing of its own.

## Sections in order

The sections run top to bottom in this order. **Blend** and **Motion Blur** are rows inside Transform.

| Section | What it's for | Shown for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Transform](/canvas/transform/) | Scale, position, rotation, opacity, [blend](/canvas/blend-modes/) and [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) | Every clip that draws |
| [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) | Drawing a clip behind the person in the shot | Every clip that draws except adjustment and nest clips, and only while no nest is open |
| [Layout](/framing/layout-section/) | How a camera and a screen recording share the frame | One selected clip of a movie with a known picture size |

---
title: Position, scale, rotation and opacity
description: Set a clip's exact size, place, angle and transparency in the Transform section, or make it fit or fill the canvas.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Transform section holds the numbers behind a clip's place in the frame. Use it when you want an exact value, or when a button can do the work of a drag.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform', 'Handles on the canvas']}
  tools="set_video"
/>

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Transform section at its defaults: Scale 100.0%, Position X 0 px, Position Y 0 px, Rotation 0.0°, Opacity 100%, Blend Normal and Motion Blur 0%, with the Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas buttons underneath."
/>

## The Transform section

Every clip that draws has Transform, text and shapes included, and it's the one section on the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) that starts open. Closed, its summary reads the scale, and the rotation when there is one: `150% · 45°`.

| Row | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Scale** | The clip's size | 100 % | 1 to 1000 % | 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 400 |
| **Position X** | Distance right of the canvas centre | 0 px | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
| **Position Y** | Distance below the canvas centre | 0 px | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
| **Rotation** | The clip's angle | 0° | −180° to 180° | −90, −45, 0, 45, 90, 180 |
| **Opacity** | How solid the clip is | 100 % | 0 to 100 % | 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 |
| **Blend** | How the clip combines with what's under it. See [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/). | Normal | Eight modes | |
| **Motion Blur** | Smear on fast movement. See [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/). | 0 % | 0 to 100 % | 0, 25, 50, 100 |

Under the rows are [Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas](#fit-and-fill). [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers typing in a field, its slider and its quick picks.

To do the same by hand on the picture, see [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).

## Scale

At 100 % a video or picture draws at its native pixels, one source pixel to one canvas pixel, so a 1920 × 1080 clip on a 3840 × 2160 canvas covers a quarter of it. The field takes one decimal place.

Scale pivots on the centre of the uncropped picture. It works on video, image, text, shape and graphic clips.

## Position

Position places the clip's centre in canvas pixels, measured from the centre of the canvas. At 0, 0 the clip sits in the middle. **Position X** runs right and **Position Y** runs down, so negative values go left and up.

Both are typed fields in whole pixels, with no slider. On a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip they still measure the centre of the uncropped picture.

## Rotation

Rotation turns the clip about its centre, and a positive angle turns it clockwise on screen. The field takes one decimal place.

## Opacity

Opacity sets how see-through the clip is: at 100 % it's solid, and at 0 % it's fully transparent.

## Fit and fill

Both buttons scale each selected clip and centre it, setting its position to 0, 0.

- **Fit to Canvas** makes the whole picture fit inside the canvas, so you may see the background at two edges.
- **Fill Canvas** makes the picture cover the whole canvas, so its edges may run off two sides.

Each clip gets its own scale from its own size, and all of them together are one undo step. A shape uses its box, a graphic its size and a nest its own canvas.

Good to know:

- Text clips are skipped, because their size comes from the words. So is any clip with no known size. If that leaves nothing to scale, Frame Job beeps.
- Both buttons measure the uncropped picture, so a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip can leave a gap after **Fill Canvas**.
- Rotation stays as it is and isn't counted, so a rotated clip may not fit or fill the way it would upright.
- A scale past the 1 to 1000 % range isn't applied, so a very small picture on a large canvas can get an error from **Fill Canvas** instead.

## Reset

**Reset** in the section's header puts position, scale, rotation, opacity, blend and motion blur back to their defaults in one step. It shows only while the section differs from its default.

It leaves the [crop](/canvas/crop/) alone, which has its own **Reset**. To put back a single row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.

## Animate these values

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, Scale, Position, Rotation, Opacity and Motion Blur set the action's end state, and the clip ramps there along the action's curve. Blend switches at the action's end instead. **Reset** gives way to **Clear**, which takes the section out of the action.

See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## No stretching

Scale is uniform for pictures. A video, image, graphic or nest always keeps its proportions, and there's no separate width and height.

Only two kinds of clip can change on one axis: a shape, through its box's width and height, and text, through its wrap width. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) and [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/).

## Related

- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)
- [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/)
- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/)

---
title: Blend modes
description: Choose how a layer combines with what's under it, and understand why a blend can look like it isn't working.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A blend mode decides how a layer's colours combine with whatever is already on the canvas under it. Use one to lay a glow over a shot, darken with a texture, or mix two pictures.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend" tools="set_video" />

## The Blend popup

<Steps>

1. Put the layer you want to blend on a track in front of something to blend with.

2. Select it and open the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/).

3. In **Transform**, choose a mode from the **Blend** popup.

</Steps>

Every clip starts on **Normal**. The change is one undo step, and with several clips selected it applies to all of them.

Hover over the popup for a reminder of what a blend needs behind it.

## The eight modes

These are in the popup's order. "Underneath" means every layer behind this one, and the canvas background.

| Mode | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Normal** | Draws over what's underneath. |
| **Multiply** | Darkens, by multiplying with what's underneath. |
| **Screen** | Lightens, the inverse of Multiply. A screened white blob reads as a glow. |
| **Add** | Adds the colours together. |
| **Overlay** | Multiplies where what's underneath is dark, and screens where it's light. |
| **Darken** | Keeps the darker of the two colours. |
| **Lighten** | Keeps the lighter of the two colours. |
| **Difference** | Gives the absolute difference of the two colours. |

## Nothing behind

A blend needs something under the layer, and over the empty black canvas it can't do much:

| Mode | Over the empty black canvas |
| --- | --- |
| **Multiply**, **Darken**, **Overlay** | The layer reads black. |
| **Screen**, **Add**, **Lighten**, **Difference** | The layer looks unchanged. |

The Transform section warns you when that's what's happening, for example "Nothing behind this clip — multiply reads black here." or "Nothing behind this clip — add changes nothing here."

The note looks at the clip's whole span, not only the frame at the playhead, so anything behind any part of the clip stands it down. Hidden tracks don't count, and neither do clips with their video turned off. It reads the first selected clip.

It appears only while the canvas background is opaque black. Over a transparent canvas, a blend draws the layer untouched.

To give the layer something to blend against:

- Use **Clip ▸ Add Background** to put a plate on a new track at the back. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
- Set a non-black colour under [Canvas background](/projects/background-and-timecode/) on the Document tab.

## During a transition

A layer always draws as **Normal** for as long as it's in a [transition](/motion/transitions/), whatever blend mode it has. The popup keeps showing the clip's own mode during the overlap. Only the frames in the overlap draw as Normal.

## Animate a blend mode

An [action](/motion/actions/) can change the mode. It doesn't ramp from one to the other: it holds, then switches at the action's end, and the row shows `at end` while you're editing that action.

## Good to know

- **Nest clips.** The popup is greyed on a nest clip, with the note "A nest has no pixels of its own to blend — un-group it (⇧⌘G) to blend the clips inside." Use **Clip ▸ Un-nest**, blend the clip you wanted, and nest again.
- **Clips inside a nest.** You can blend a clip inside a nest. It blends against the canvas below the whole nest, not against the nest's own clips under it.
- **Adjustment clips.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) takes no blend mode.
- **Matte tracks.** A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) keeps its blend mode, but it has no effect while the track is a matte.
- **Encoded or linear light.** A project can blend in either. See [Blending: encoded or linear light](/hdr/blending/).

## Related

- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)
- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)

- **Matte tracks.** A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) keeps its blend mode, but it has no effect while the track is a matte.
- **Encoded or linear light.** A project can blend in either. See [Blending: encoded or linear light](/hdr/blending/).

---
title: Corner radius
description: Round the corners of a video, image or still clip, from a soft edge to a pill or a circle.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Corner radius rounds the corners of a picture, which is handy for a picture-in-picture or a screen recording sitting on a background.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Corner Radius ▸ Radius" tools="set_video" />

## Round the corners

<Steps>

1. Select a video, image or still clip and open the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/).

2. Open the **Corner Radius** section.

3. Drag **Radius**, type a value, or choose a quick pick.

</Steps>

| Row | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Radius** | How round the corners are, in source pixels | 0 px | 0 to 500 px | 0, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 |

Closed, the section's summary reads the radius, such as `32 px`. **Reset** appears in its header while the radius isn't 0.

## How the radius is measured

The radius is in the source's own pixels, so it scales with the clip. A radius of 32 px on a clip at 50 % looks like 16 px on the canvas.

It rounds the [cropped](/canvas/crop/) picture, so the curve follows the crop rather than the original frame. A [shadow](/effects/shadow/) follows the rounded shape.

A radius can't be more than half the picture's shorter side, and anything above that draws as that half. So a big enough radius turns a wide picture into a pill and a square picture into a circle.

## Animate the radius

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Radius** sets the action's end state, and the corners ramp there along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## Good to know

Only video, image and still clips have this section. A rectangle shape has its own radius: see [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).

## Related

- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
- [The Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/)
