---
title: Crop
description: Trim a picture's edges by dragging handles on the canvas or by typing an exact number of pixels.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Crop cuts pixels off the edges of a video, image or still clip. Drag the edges on the canvas when you're working by eye, or type the amounts when you need them exact.

<AtAGlance
  keys="C"
  where={['Double-click a clip in the preview', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Crop']}
  tools="set_video"
/>

## Crop mode

Crop mode turns the handles on the canvas into crop edges.

<Steps>

1. Select the clip, with the playhead somewhere it's showing.

2. Press <kbd>C</kbd>, double-click the clip in the preview, or choose **Crop on Canvas** in the Crop section.

3. Drag the [crop handles](#crop-handles).

4. Press <kbd>↩</kbd> to [leave crop mode](#leaving-crop-mode).

</Steps>

<kbd>C</kbd> beeps when no selected clip is showing at the playhead, because there's nothing on the canvas to crop. Double-clicking a text clip opens its text editor instead.

Going in and out of crop mode isn't an edit, so it adds nothing to undo.

## Crop handles

In crop mode the eight square handles become crop edges and the rotation grip goes away. A corner handle moves two edges, and a side handle moves one.

What you're cutting away shows as a dim ghost, inside a dashed outline of the uncropped frame.

- A drag changes the crop and nothing else. The clip's position stays put, and the picture doesn't shift.
- A crop drag doesn't snap.
- At least one source pixel always remains in each direction, however far you drag.
- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during a drag to cancel it. The crop goes back to where it was, with no undo step.
- Each finished drag is one undo step.

Dragging inside the box still moves the clip, as it does outside crop mode. With several clips selected, the handles belong to the front-most one and crop only that clip.

## Leaving crop mode

Your crop stays when you leave. Any of these leaves crop mode:

| Do this | Good to know |
| --- | --- |
| Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Needs the canvas to have focus. |
| Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Needs the canvas to have focus. During a drag, the first <kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels the drag and the next one leaves the mode. |
| Press <kbd>C</kbd> or choose **Crop on Canvas** | Works wherever the focus is, except while you're typing in a field. |
| Click empty canvas | This also clears the selection, unless you hold <kbd>⇧</kbd>. |
| Click a different clip on the canvas | That clip becomes the selection. |

The canvas has focus once you've clicked or dragged on it. If you pressed <kbd>C</kbd> and haven't touched the canvas yet, press <kbd>C</kbd> again to leave.

Crop mode also ends if nothing selected is left on the canvas, for example when you clear the selection in the timeline.

## The Crop section

The **Crop** section on the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) has the same four edges as fields, for when you want an exact number. It shows only for video, image and still clips.

| Field | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Left** | Source pixels cut from the left edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
| **Top** | Source pixels cut from the top edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
| **Right** | Source pixels cut from the right edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
| **Bottom** | Source pixels cut from the bottom edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |

These are typed fields, with no slider. **Crop on Canvas** under them goes in and out of crop mode.

Closed, the section's summary reads `none`, or the four amounts in field order, such as `100·0·100·0`. **Reset** appears in the section's header while there's a crop, and takes all four edges back to 0.

Left and Right together must stay under the picture's width, and Top and Bottom under its height. If a number would use up the whole picture, Frame Job shows an error and keeps the crop you had.

:::caution
With several clips selected, editing one field gives every clip all four of the first clip's amounts, not only the edge you changed. Crop clips of different sizes one at a time.
:::

## How a crop works

A crop removes edges in place. The picture you keep stays exactly where it was on the canvas, so cropping the left edge opens a gap on the left rather than sliding the picture over.

The amounts are in the source's own pixels, not canvas pixels, so they stay correct when you scale the clip later. Cutting 100 px from a clip at 50 % takes 50 canvas pixels off it, and the same 100 px at 200 % takes 200.

Position, scale and rotation go on measuring from the centre of the uncropped picture. A crop doesn't recentre what's left, so move the clip if you want that.

- [Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas](/canvas/transform/#fit-and-fill) measure the uncropped picture too.
- [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/) and the [shadow](/effects/shadow/) follow the cropped edge.
- [Reset in Transform](/canvas/transform/#reset) leaves the crop alone.

## Animate a crop

A crop can change over time. With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected on a single clip, a crop handle or a field sets the crop at the action's end, and the edges move there along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

While you're editing an action, the section's **Reset** gives way to **Clear**, which takes the crop out of that action.

## Good to know

- Crop mode has no menu item. It's <kbd>C</kbd>, a double-click, or the **Crop on Canvas** button.
- <kbd>C</kbd> also opens crop mode on a text, shape, graphic or nest clip, and a double-click does on all of those except text. They have no Crop section, so there are no fields and no **Reset**. To take that crop off, undo or drag the handles back.
- A clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) shows no crop handles.

## Related

- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)
- [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/)
- [The Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/)

---
title: The Picture tab
description: Find every section of the Clip tab's Picture sub-tab, see which clips get which section, and learn how the sections behave.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Picture tab is where you place a clip in the frame and style what it draws. It's one sub-tab of the inspector's **Clip** tab, and the sections it shows depend on what you've selected.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture" tools="set_video" />

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with a video clip selected and its Picture sub-tab chosen beside Color, Sound and Clip. The Transform section is open, with rows for Scale, Position X, Position Y, Rotation, Opacity, Blend and Motion Blur, then the Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas buttons. Behind Subject and Layout sit below it."
/>

## Open the Picture tab

Select a clip, open the inspector's **Clip** tab and choose **Picture**. A video or image clip opens on it, while a text clip opens on **Text**, a shape on **Shape** and a graphic on **Graphic**.

The sub-tabs you get depend on the clip:

| Selected | Sub-tabs |
| --- | --- |
| Video clip | Picture, Color, Sound, Clip |
| Image or still clip | Picture, Color, Clip |
| Text clip | Text, Picture, Clip |
| Shape clip | Shape, Picture, Clip |
| Graphic clip | Graphic, Picture, Clip |
| Nest clip | Picture, Clip |
| Adjustment clip | Color, Clip |
| Clip of an audio-only file | Sound, Clip |

**Sound** joins the list for any clip with live audio, so a video clip with no sound doesn't have it and a nest with sound inside does.

A selection with an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) in it has no Picture tab, because an adjustment clip draws nothing of its own.

## Sections in order

The sections run top to bottom in this order. **Blend** and **Motion Blur** are rows inside Transform.

| Section | What it's for | Shown for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Transform](/canvas/transform/) | Scale, position, rotation, opacity, [blend](/canvas/blend-modes/) and [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) | Every clip that draws |
| [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) | Drawing a clip behind the person in the shot | Every clip that draws except adjustment and nest clips, and only while no nest is open |
| [Layout](/framing/layout-section/) | How a camera and a screen recording share the frame | One selected clip of a movie with a known picture size |
| [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) | Showing a clip only while a sound plays | Every clip that draws except nests |
| [Crop](/canvas/crop/) | Trimming the picture's edges | Video, image and still clips |
| [Corner Radius](/canvas/corner-radius/) | Rounding the picture's corners | Video, image and still clips |
| [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/) | Keying out a green screen | Video, image and still clips |
| [Background](/effects/remove-background/) | Removing the background behind a person or subject | Clips of a video file, freeze frames of one, and image clips |
| [Cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) | Styling a recorded pointer | Clips of a movie with a cursor file its picture doesn't already show |
| [Shadow](/effects/shadow/) | A drop shadow | Every clip that draws |
| [Filters](/effects/filters/) | A stack of up to four filters | Every clip that draws |
| [Reflection](/effects/reflection/) | A mirror image under the clip | Every clip that draws |
| [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) | Darkening everything but one area | Every clip that draws |
| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) | Hiding regions of the picture | Every clip that draws |

Every clip that draws includes text, shapes, graphics and nests. A section that doesn't apply isn't there at all, rather than greyed out. With several clips selected, a section shows only when it applies to all of them.

A graphic clip can be moved, scaled, faded and blended here. It has no Crop, Corner Radius or Chroma Key, and no Color tab.

## How sections behave

**Fold a section.** Click its header to open or close it. Transform starts open and the rest start closed, and Frame Job remembers what you open and close. A closed section still shows a short summary of its settings.

**Reset a section.** **Reset** appears in a section's header only while the section differs from its default. It puts the whole section back. To put back a single row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.

**Edit several clips at once.** With several clips selected, a field shows the first clip's value, with a `mixed` badge when the others differ. An edit applies to every selected clip.

**Pick a colour.** A colour swatch opens the macOS Colors panel, with opacity.

**Edit inside an action.** With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, the rows read and write the action's end state, and the sections it animates open by themselves. **Reset** gives way to **Clear**, which takes that section out of the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

[Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers typing, sliders and the quick picks in a field's menu.

## With an agent

`set_video` changes a clip's placement and look by merging a patch into each clip's properties, for as many clips as you name. An agent's value outside a range gets an error rather than being pulled back into the range, and animating a property takes an action. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Good to know

A nest clip has no picture of its own, so most of this tab doesn't reach it. Position, scale, rotation and opacity apply to the clips inside. Blend is greyed, and Shadow, Filters, Reflection, Spotlight and Obscure show but have no effect on the nest clip. Set those on the clips inside the [nest](/editing/nests/). A nest's opacity fades each clip inside separately, rather than the group as one picture.

## Related

- [The inspector](/getting-started/inspector/)
- [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/)
- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)

---
title: Position, scale, rotation and opacity
description: Set a clip's exact size, place, angle and transparency in the Transform section, or make it fit or fill the canvas.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Transform section holds the numbers behind a clip's place in the frame. Use it when you want an exact value, or when a button can do the work of a drag.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform', 'Handles on the canvas']}
  tools="set_video"
/>

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Transform section at its defaults: Scale 100.0%, Position X 0 px, Position Y 0 px, Rotation 0.0°, Opacity 100%, Blend Normal and Motion Blur 0%, with the Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas buttons underneath."
/>

## The Transform section

Every clip that draws has Transform, text and shapes included, and it's the one section on the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) that starts open. Closed, its summary reads the scale, and the rotation when there is one: `150% · 45°`.

| Row | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Scale** | The clip's size | 100 % | 1 to 1000 % | 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 400 |
| **Position X** | Distance right of the canvas centre | 0 px | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
| **Position Y** | Distance below the canvas centre | 0 px | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
| **Rotation** | The clip's angle | 0° | −180° to 180° | −90, −45, 0, 45, 90, 180 |
| **Opacity** | How solid the clip is | 100 % | 0 to 100 % | 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 |
| **Blend** | How the clip combines with what's under it. See [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/). | Normal | Eight modes | |
| **Motion Blur** | Smear on fast movement. See [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/). | 0 % | 0 to 100 % | 0, 25, 50, 100 |

Under the rows are [Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas](#fit-and-fill). [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers typing in a field, its slider and its quick picks.

To do the same by hand on the picture, see [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).

## Scale

At 100 % a video or picture draws at its native pixels, one source pixel to one canvas pixel, so a 1920 × 1080 clip on a 3840 × 2160 canvas covers a quarter of it. The field takes one decimal place.

Scale pivots on the centre of the uncropped picture. It works on video, image, text, shape and graphic clips.

## Position

Position places the clip's centre in canvas pixels, measured from the centre of the canvas. At 0, 0 the clip sits in the middle. **Position X** runs right and **Position Y** runs down, so negative values go left and up.

Both are typed fields in whole pixels, with no slider. On a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip they still measure the centre of the uncropped picture.

## Rotation

Rotation turns the clip about its centre, and a positive angle turns it clockwise on screen. The field takes one decimal place.

## Opacity

Opacity sets how see-through the clip is: at 100 % it's solid, and at 0 % it's fully transparent.

## Fit and fill

Both buttons scale each selected clip and centre it, setting its position to 0, 0.

- **Fit to Canvas** makes the whole picture fit inside the canvas, so you may see the background at two edges.
- **Fill Canvas** makes the picture cover the whole canvas, so its edges may run off two sides.

Each clip gets its own scale from its own size, and all of them together are one undo step. A shape uses its box, a graphic its size and a nest its own canvas.

Good to know:

- Text clips are skipped, because their size comes from the words. So is any clip with no known size. If that leaves nothing to scale, Frame Job beeps.
- Both buttons measure the uncropped picture, so a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip can leave a gap after **Fill Canvas**.
- Rotation stays as it is and isn't counted, so a rotated clip may not fit or fill the way it would upright.
- A scale past the 1 to 1000 % range isn't applied, so a very small picture on a large canvas can get an error from **Fill Canvas** instead.

## Reset

**Reset** in the section's header puts position, scale, rotation, opacity, blend and motion blur back to their defaults in one step. It shows only while the section differs from its default.

It leaves the [crop](/canvas/crop/) alone, which has its own **Reset**. To put back a single row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.

## Animate these values

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, Scale, Position, Rotation, Opacity and Motion Blur set the action's end state, and the clip ramps there along the action's curve. Blend switches at the action's end instead. **Reset** gives way to **Clear**, which takes the section out of the action.

See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## No stretching

Scale is uniform for pictures. A video, image, graphic or nest always keeps its proportions, and there's no separate width and height.

Only two kinds of clip can change on one axis: a shape, through its box's width and height, and text, through its wrap width. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) and [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/).

## Related

- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)
- [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/)
- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/)

---
title: Blend modes
description: Choose how a layer combines with what's under it, and understand why a blend can look like it isn't working.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A blend mode decides how a layer's colours combine with whatever is already on the canvas under it. Use one to lay a glow over a shot, darken with a texture, or mix two pictures.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend" tools="set_video" />

## The Blend popup

<Steps>

1. Put the layer you want to blend on a track in front of something to blend with.

2. Select it and open the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/).

3. In **Transform**, choose a mode from the **Blend** popup.

</Steps>

Every clip starts on **Normal**. The change is one undo step, and with several clips selected it applies to all of them.

Hover over the popup for a reminder of what a blend needs behind it.

## The eight modes

These are in the popup's order. "Underneath" means every layer behind this one, and the canvas background.

| Mode | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Normal** | Draws over what's underneath. |
| **Multiply** | Darkens, by multiplying with what's underneath. |
| **Screen** | Lightens, the inverse of Multiply. A screened white blob reads as a glow. |
| **Add** | Adds the colours together. |
| **Overlay** | Multiplies where what's underneath is dark, and screens where it's light. |
| **Darken** | Keeps the darker of the two colours. |
| **Lighten** | Keeps the lighter of the two colours. |
| **Difference** | Gives the absolute difference of the two colours. |

## Nothing behind

A blend needs something under the layer, and over the empty black canvas it can't do much:

| Mode | Over the empty black canvas |
| --- | --- |
| **Multiply**, **Darken**, **Overlay** | The layer reads black. |
| **Screen**, **Add**, **Lighten**, **Difference** | The layer looks unchanged. |

The Transform section warns you when that's what's happening, for example "Nothing behind this clip — multiply reads black here." or "Nothing behind this clip — add changes nothing here."

The note looks at the clip's whole span, not only the frame at the playhead, so anything behind any part of the clip stands it down. Hidden tracks don't count, and neither do clips with their video turned off. It reads the first selected clip.

It appears only while the canvas background is opaque black. Over a transparent canvas, a blend draws the layer untouched.

To give the layer something to blend against:

- Use **Clip ▸ Add Background** to put a plate on a new track at the back. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
- Set a non-black colour under [Canvas background](/projects/background-and-timecode/) on the Document tab.

## During a transition

A layer always draws as **Normal** for as long as it's in a [transition](/motion/transitions/), whatever blend mode it has. The popup keeps showing the clip's own mode during the overlap. Only the frames in the overlap draw as Normal.

## Animate a blend mode

An [action](/motion/actions/) can change the mode. It doesn't ramp from one to the other: it holds, then switches at the action's end, and the row shows `at end` while you're editing that action.

## Good to know

- **Nest clips.** The popup is greyed on a nest clip, with the note "A nest has no pixels of its own to blend — un-group it (⇧⌘G) to blend the clips inside." Use **Clip ▸ Un-nest**, blend the clip you wanted, and nest again.
- **Clips inside a nest.** You can blend a clip inside a nest. It blends against the canvas below the whole nest, not against the nest's own clips under it.
- **Adjustment clips.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) takes no blend mode.
- **Matte tracks.** A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) keeps its blend mode, but it has no effect while the track is a matte.
- **Encoded or linear light.** A project can blend in either. See [Blending: encoded or linear light](/hdr/blending/).

## Related

- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)
- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)

A radius can't be more than half the picture's shorter side, and anything above that draws as that half. So a big enough radius turns a wide picture into a pill and a square picture into a circle.

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Radius** sets the action's end state, and the corners ramp there along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## Good to know

Only video, image and still clips have this section. A rectangle shape has its own radius: see [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).

## Related

- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
- [The Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/)

### Hide while silent

A camera clip can fade out while nobody is talking and fade back in just before
speech starts. Select the camera and open the Clip tab's Picture sub-tab: the
**Hide While Silent** section comes after Layout, shut until you open it. It is
offered for any clip with a picture but a nest clip (set it on the clips inside

### Reflection

**Mirror the layer below itself** hangs a mirrored copy under the layer. The
reflection rotates with the layer, and the layer always draws over its own
reflection.

| Row | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Opacity | 0–100 % | 35 % |
| Height | 0–100 % of the layer's height | 50 % |
| Gap | 0–200 px | 0 px |
| Falloff | 0–100 % | 100 % |

### Spotlight

**Spotlight a region** dims the canvas outside a rectangle or ellipse on the
clip, and can magnify what is inside.

| Row | Range | Default |
### Obscure

Obscure hides a face, a password field or a phone number behind up to **four**
blurred or pixelated regions per clip.

- **Add Region** adds a 480 × 270 pixelated box at the centre of the layer.
- **Place on Canvas** arms a drawing mode ("Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc
  to cancel"). Drag a rectangle over the selected clip to add a region there.
